from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines_text = ["Vectors possess both magnitude and direction.", "Scalars are represented by single numbers.", "Think of vectors as directed paths."]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: What is a Vector?", lecture_lines_text)
        
        # Define objects
        origin = Dot(point=np.array([2.0, 2.0, 0]), color=WHITE)
        target_point = Dot(point=self.grid["B4"], color=WHITE)
        vector = Arrow(start=origin.get_center(), end=target_point.get_center(), color="#FF5733", buff=0)
        label_v = Text("Vector V", font_size=24, color="#FF5733")
        label_v.next_to(target_point, UP, buff=0.1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.play(Create(target_point), Create(origin))
        self.play(Create(vector), Write(label_v))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        # Pulsing effect for magnitude
        self.play(vector.animate.scale(1.2).set_color("#FFFF00"), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(vector.animate.scale(1/1.2).set_color("#FF5733"), run_time=0.5)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        # Highlight origin and point
        h_origin = Circle(radius=0.2, color="#FFFF00").move_to(origin)
        h_point = Circle(radius=0.2, color="#FFFF00").move_to(target_point)
        self.play(Create(h_origin), Create(h_point))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Vectors in 2D Space", ["Vectors are arrows on a plane.", "Each starts at the origin point.", "Coordinates define the vector's position."])

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Rule", [
            "Vector addition combines two vectors.",
            "Place second tail at first tip.",
            "Resultant is the path's total displacement."
        ])
        
        origin = self.grid['E2']
        vec_a_end = origin + np.array([1.6, 0.8, 0])
        vec_b_end = vec_a_end + np.array([0.8, 2.4, 0])
        
        vec_a = Arrow(origin, vec_a_end, color="#2ECC71", buff=0)
        vec_b = Arrow(vec_a_end, vec_b_end, color="#F1C40F", buff=0)
        res_vec = Arrow(origin, vec_b_end, color="#FFFFFF", buff=0)
        
        label_a = MathTex(r"\vec{a}", color="#2ECC71").next_to(vec_a.get_center(), UP)
        label_b = MathTex(r"\vec{b}", color="#F1C40F").next_to(vec_b.get_center(), RIGHT)
        label_res = MathTex(r"\vec{a}+\vec{b}", color="#FFFFFF").next_to(res_vec.get_center(), LEFT)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#2ECC71"))
        self.play(Create(vec_a), Write(label_a))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Scalars scale vector magnitude.", "Multiplying by two doubles reach.", "Negative values reverse the direction."]
        self.setup_layout("Scalar Multiplication", lecture_lines)
        
        # Axes
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.6)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        v2_coords = [2, 4]
        v2 = Vector(axes.c2p(*v2_coords), color="#E74C3C")

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        v3 = Vector(axes.c2p(*v3_coords), color="#9B59B6")

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion & Real-World Application", ["Vectors build our digital world.", "Linear algebra enables game physics.", "Machine learning uses vector spaces."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show an icon representing a physical force vector. Color in #FFFFFF.
        force_vector = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT*1.5, color="#FFFFFF")
        label1 = Text("Force Vector", font_size=20, color="#FFFFFF").next_to(force_vector, UP)
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(force_vector, label1), 'B5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(force_vector), Write(label1))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate vectors combining to represent velocity in a game. Color in #FF5733.
        v1 = Arrow(ORIGIN, UP*1 + RIGHT*1, color="#FF5733")
        v2 = Arrow(ORIGIN, DOWN*0.5 + RIGHT*1.5, color="#FF5733")
        v_sum = Arrow(ORIGIN, UP*0.5 + RIGHT*2.5, color="#FF5733", buff=0)
        label2 = Text("Resultant Velocity", font_size=20, color="#FF5733").next_to(v_sum, DOWN)
        
        group = VGroup(v1, v2, v_sum, label2)
        self.place_in_area(group, 'D4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        self.play(Create(v1), Create(v2))
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(VGroup(v1.copy(), v2.copy()), v_sum))
        self.play(Write(label2))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF5733")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display text: 'Vectors are essential for physics and graphics'. Color in #2ECC71.
        msg = Text("Vectors are essential for physics and graphics", font_size=24, color="#2ECC71")
        self.place_at_grid(msg, 'F4', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(msg))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#2ECC71")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Fundamentals of Vectors: The Language of Space

sections.title: Introduction: What is a Vector?
sections.content: Define a vector not just as a list of numbers, but as an entity possessing both magnitude and direction. Contrast this with 'scalars' (single numbers).
sections.example: A drone flying: The speed (5 m/s) is a scalar, but the path (North-East at 5 m/s) is a vector.

sections.title: Visualizing Vectors in 2D Space
sections.content: Represent vectors as directed arrows on a Cartesian plane starting from the origin. Explain the coordinate representation (x, y).
sections.example: An arrow starting at (0,0) and ending at (3,2). Visualize it as moving 3 units right and 2 units up.

sections.title: Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Rule
sections.content: Explain how to combine two vectors. Introduce the 'tip-to-tail' method where the tail of the second vector starts at the tip of the first.
sections.example: A cat walks 2 meters East, then 3 meters North. The resultant vector is the straight line from the starting point to the final position.

sections.title: Scalar Multiplication: Stretching and Flipping
sections.content: Discuss what happens when you multiply a vector by a number. A scalar changes the magnitude (stretching/shrinking) and can reverse the direction if negative.
sections.example: A robot arm extending: Multiplying the vector (1, 1) by a factor of 2 results in (2, 2), effectively doubling its reach.

sections.title: Conclusion & Real-World Application
sections.content: Summarize how these building blocks (addition/scaling) form the basis of Linear Algebra used in game physics, machine learning, and computer graphics.
sections.example: In video games, thousands of tiny vectors are added together to calculate the movement of characters across a 3D landscape.
